title: Elastic token-pool bursting allocator & tenant-aware ingress playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: Over the last quarter we've observed repeated p99+ spikes and transient 429/5xx behavior on the embeddings endpoint during bursty multi-tenant load (customer search reindexing, large-batch vectorization jobs). Root causes identified in preliminary analysis: single global inbound queue saturation, cold warm-pool spin-ups underburst, fixed per-tenant static rate limits that underutilize available capacity, and autoscaler thresholds tuned for steady-state QPS rather than burst elasticity. This ticket implements an operational + runtime solution: a burstable token pool allocator with tenant-aware admission, a reservoir-based soft-reservation layer for short bursts, and cost-aware autoscaler tuning to reduce tail latency without disproportionate cost increase.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end p99 latency for embeddings reduces by >=30% for burst windows (1m windows) versus baseline; 2) Transient 429s during known burst events reduced by >=80%; 3) Average token-based cost change <= +7% (target neutral); 4) No regression for steady-state throughput; 5) Automated canary rollout with circuit-breaker that can rollback to previous behavior within 5 minutes; 6) Observability: dashboards displaying token pool utilization, per-tenant admission rejections, autoscaler decisions, and warm-pool occupancy are live and alerting thresholds configured.
rollout_plan: Phase A (experiments, 2 weeks): implement server-side admission controller and synthetic load harness to validate algorithms; run offline sims with historical traces. Phase B (internal canary, 1 week): deploy admission controller + reservoir on a low-risk region and route 5% of tenants, verify metrics and cost. Phase C (gradual ramp, 2 weeks): expand to 30% then 70% with automated safety checks; enable warm-pool preallocation for top-50 tenants. Phase D (full roll): switch global routing policy to tenant-aware admission. Post-roll: 2 weeks of heightened monitoring, runbook exercised. Rollback criteria: sustained p99 increase >10% or error rate >0.2% over 5m.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Use reservoir-based soft reservations rather than strict static burst buckets to favor common-case single-tenant burst usage while preserving multi-tenant fairness. Pro: better tail latency for bursty customers. Con: slightly more complex bookkeeping and potential headroom fragmentation.
- Autoscaler tuned for 95th-percentile burst targets (short window) instead of mean usage to reduce cold-start tail latency; tradeoff is increased short-term cost for pre-warming. We mitigate via warm-pool intelligent sizing and cost caps.
- Backpressure signal will be exposed to SDKs via Retry-After and a new 'admission_hint' header to enable client-side exponential backoff — non-breaking and optional.
- Rate limits moved from strictly per-tenant static tokens to a two-tier scheme: guaranteed baseline and a shared-burst reservoir with weighted fairness (weights derived from committed tiers).
implementation_notes:
- Admission controller component to live in ingress layer (serving-router) with low-latency in-memory token accounting and persistent metrics exported via Prometheus.
- Warm pools implemented as reserved GPU slots flagged 'embedding-warm' with accelerated initialization paths.
- Autoscaler changes: add burst window (60s) targets, headroom buffer parameter, and respect cost ceilings per-cluster.
- SDK changes: add optional backoff-friendly hooks to respect admission_hint and expose per-request identifiers for tracing.
- Data collection: instrument per-tenant queueing time, token consumption rate, reservoir usage fraction, warm-pool hit rate, and autoscaler decision traces.
instrumentation: Dashboards: Embeddings > Ingress token pool (utilization, reservoir fill), Per-tenant QoS (rejections, retries), Autoscaler decisions (scale events, reason), Warm-pool occupancy. Alerts: Reservoir depleted (>=3m), p99 increase >10% over baseline (5m), 429 rate >0.1% (5m), Autoscaler flapping (>=3 scales in 10m). Links below.
